Let me analyze these teaching examples carefully to identify systematic errors in the model forecasts compared to true outcomes.

Looking at the examples, I need to compare:
1. Model forecasts (30-day horizon)
2. True outcomes (30-day horizon)
3. The sentiment history
4. The price history

Let me analyze each example:

**Example 1 (2024-11-11)** - This is after a price increase from the low 60s to the high 60s range.

History: 63.03 → 62.98 → 62.28 → 61.76 → 62.25 → 64.89 → 66.63 → 66.97 → 66.40 → 67.28 → 65.47 → 64.58 → 63.87 → 65.22 → 64.30 → 63.76 → 66.04 → 68.02

The price has been rising, with the latest at 68.02 on 2024-11-11.

Model forecasts at day 0: 67.46
True outcome at day 0: 67.57

Looking at the divergence pattern:

Model forecasts seem to be somewhat below the true outcomes in many cases. Let me look at the first few days:

Day 0: Model 67.46 vs True 67.57 (underestimated by 0.11)
Day 1: Model 67.49 vs True 67.53 (underestimated by 0.04)
Day 2: Model 66.35 vs True 66.31 (overestimated by -0.04, so model was higher)
Day 3: Model 68.07 vs True 68.27 (underestimated by 0.20)
Day 4: Model 67.86 vs True 68.01 (underestimated by 0.15)
Day 5: Model 69.28 vs True 69.51 (underestimated by 0.23)


Day 6: Model 67.88 vs True 68.13 (underestimated by 0.25)
Day 7: Model 67.90 vs True 68.38 (underestimated by 0.48)
Day 8: Model 69.46 vs True 69.99 (underestimated by 0.53)
